text: This video shows how to record a program and replay it.
doeff is a library for algebraic effects in Python.
We follow latest_releases, which asks GitHub for tags.
A program asks the world questions and gets answers.
Write down each question with its answer.
Later, answer the same questions from those notes.
The program runs the same way, with nobody on the other end.
In doeff, a question is a value. Here it is HttpRequest.
It holds a method, a URL and headers.
latest_releases starts with an empty dict of tags.
For each repository, it yields an HttpRequest.
It pauses there. A handler gets the request and its k.
k is the rest of the function, and it resumes once.
With the body back, it keeps the tag_name.
Then it returns the tags.
github counts each request it gets as sent.
It finds the repository in the URL.
It resumes that k with a body, as the API would.
Run it under github: two requests, two tags.
And sent says 2.
Now put recording(tape) between them.
record yields the same request on, and github answers.
It keeps the answer in the tape, then resumes that k.
Then take github away, and run under replaying(tape).
replay finds each request in the tape and answers it.
Same tags, and sent stays at 0.
latest_releases never changed. Only the handlers did.
